title: Hydrogen Storage, Optoelectronic, and Thermoelectric characteristics of Lithium-Based Perovskite Hydrides LiXH3 (X = Be-Ba): First-Principles Insights for Sustainable Energy Technologies

segments.text: This study utilized the DFT model, based on Material Studio and Wien2k codes, to analyze the structural, electronic, mechanical, optical, thermodynamic, and thermo-electronic properties of perovskite hydrides LiXH3 (X = Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, and Ba) for hydrogen storage capacity and sustainable energy applications.

LiBeH3, LiMgH3, LiCaH3, LiSrH3, and LiBaH3 have lattice constants of 4.39490 & Aring;, 4.51741 & Aring;, 6.27661 & Aring;, and 4.80 & Aring;, respectively, and are stable in the triclinic (P1) phase under atmospheric pressure and temperature.
Among these, LiBeH3 has the highest hydrogen storage capacity at 15.94 %, while LiMgH3, LiCaH3, LiSrH3, and LiBaH3 exhibit values of 8.82 %, 6.04 %, 3.10 %, and 2.05 %, respectively.

The electronic band structures and density of states of LiBeH3, LiMgH3, LiCaH3, LiSrH3, and LiBaH3 show semiconducting characteristics with band gap values of 2.98 eV, 2.60 eV, 2.08 eV, 1.87 eV, and 1.23 eV, respectively.
LiBeH3 demonstrates a larger Delta EHOMO-LUMO gap, indicating stronger bonding, which decreases from Be to Ba down the periodic table and facilitates rapid hydrogen desorption.
Their mechanical properties exhibit ductile behavior and notable anisotropy due to strong ionic bonds between hydrogen and metal cations and meet Born stability.

The optoelectronic potential was evaluated using various factors such as dielectric constant a (w), refractive index n (w), optical conductivity a (w), absorption coefficient a(w), and energy loss function L (w).

Furthermore, vibrational and thermodynamic stability were determined using the phonon task, as changes in specific heat capacity at constant volume (Cv), entropy (S), enthalpy (H), Helmholtz free energy (F), and Gibbs free energy (G).

BoltzTrap code was utilized to evaluate the thermoelectric properties and assess their efficiency through electrical conductivity (a), thermal conductivity (ke), Seebeck coefficient (S), power factor (S2), and figures of merit (ZT) calculations.

Therefore, high hydrogen capacities, adjustable bandgaps, mechanical and thermal stability, and outstanding optoelectronic and thermoelectric properties are significant for hydrogen storage systems, unlocking the potential of hydrogen energy and paving the way for a cleaner, greener future.

title: Production of CuAlO2 in powder, bulk and nanofiber forms

segments.text: A study was carried out on the production of CuAlO2 by using 3 different production routes namely, hydrothermal synthesis, conventional solid state reaction and electrospinning process.
For hydrothermal synthesis, commercially available metal salts, Cu2O powder and chemically precipitated CuO nanoparticles were used as precursors.
Bulk CuAlO2 samples were prepared via solid state reaction route by ball milling and high temperature sintering of CuO and Al2O3 powders.
CuAlO2 ceramic mats were synthesized by electrospinning process with the assistance of polyvinylpyrolidone, as a template polymer.
Highly crystalline mesh structured fibers were obtained after sintering of polymer/equal moles of copper chloride and aluminum nitrate composite in air.
In the current work, solid state reaction and electrospinning processes yielded phase pure CuAlO2 in hexagonal symmetry.
On the other hand, products obtained from hydrothermal synthesis were CuO, Cu2O and Al(OOH), which did not yield CuAlO2 under current experimental conditions.

Detailed qualitative X-ray diffraction analysis revealed the need of specific ionic species in the solution within a narrow temperature-composition-pH window to obtain phase pure CuAlO2 employing hydrothermal conditions.

title: A Thermogalvanic Cell Microneedle Patch for Integrated Diagnosis and Treatment of UV-Induced Early Skin Cancer

segments.text: Early stage skin cancer exhibits a high cure rate; however, conventional noninvasive screening suffers from diagnostic inaccuracies, and treatment reliant on postlesion surgery remains inherently passivity.

This work develops an all-in-one platform by coupling microneedle (MN) patches with a lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA), seamlessly integrating self-powered biomarker extraction, multimodal detection, and biomarker-responsive therapy for point-of-care testing (POCT) and personalized treatment of UV-induced early stage skin cancer.
It incorporates a thermogalvanic cell (TGC) MN, which leverages photothermal-thermoelectric coupling to achieve external power-free transdermal extraction of the biomarker (8-OH-dG) within 10 min.

The extracted 8-OH-dG triggers the structural change of the hairpin aptamer (HA) on the PtPB@PEG@HA (PPPA) nanoparticles (NPs), initiating a cascade amplification that generates abundant DNA nanozymes for colorimetric detection (100 pM to 60 nM).
A convolutional neural network (CNN) is introduced for colorimetric quantification, coupled with artificial intelligence (AI) for disease risk assessment.
Once captured in the LFIA detection zone by a capture probe, the open-loop PPPA NPs permit surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) detection of 8-OH-dG, enabling dual-mechanism cross-verification.

Under near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, the PPPA NPs also serve as photothermal actuators to trigger the controlled release of quercetin from phase-transition MNs, effectively scavenging UV-induced oxidative stress.
This innovation facilitates the home-based diagnosis and management of early stage skin cancer.

title: Giant and bidirectionally tunable ionic thermopower in Cu-based liquid flow thermocells enabled by solvation entropy for low-grade heat harvesting

segments.text: Ionic thermocells (iTCs) are promising candidates for efficiently harvesting low-grade waste heat.
Their integration inevitably requires different p/n-type redox units in series to output sufficient voltage.

However, the possible redox pairs are fairly limited, especially n-type, and furthermore the precious metals used as electrodes are commonly adopted to improve the power density, which significantly increases the complexity and cost of the integrated device.
Herein, we demonstrated a cost-effective and facile high-entropy Cu-based liquid-flow thermocell (LiTC) with giant and bidirectional ionic thermopower (Si) through tunable solvation entropy.
The Cu-based LiTCs consisted of a Y-shaped channel with Cu electrodes as the walls and CuSO4/H2SO4 injected separately from Y-shaped inlets.

The significant change in solvation entropy induced by the interaction of Cu2+ and H+/SO42- can achieve n-p conversion and present a tunable Si range of -33 similar to +2.8 mV K-1 for different CuSO4 concentrations, which are 4.7-55 times higher than those of pristine iTCs.

The Pmax/Delta T2 can reach the highest value of 1.58 mW m-2 K-2 with separate flows of 0.01 mol L-1 CuSO4 and 0.1 mol L-1 H2SO4 by using foam Cu electrodes, higher than the previous Pmax/Delta T2 records of Cu-based iTCs.

The Cu-based LiTCs with a low cost-performance metric of similar to 1.15 $ W-1 and electrolyte forced convection have great potential to realize efficient heat-to-electricity conversion and thermoregulation for high-power devices.
